title: MIMaL predicts and experimentally validates five yeast gene functions from protein–metabolite profiles
summary: MIMaL used tree-based regression and SHAP interpretation on yeast proteome/metabolome measurements, then clustered protein-control profiles across single-gene knockouts. It predicted functions for five genes, with experimental validation reported for all five. Two previously uncharacterized genes, YJR120W and YDL157C, were predicted to modulate mitochondrial translation; functions were also predicted and validated for SDH9, ISC1 and FMP52. The study additionally validated previously unrecognized protein links to citrate.
ai_technology: MIMaL: ExtraTrees regression of metabolite abundance from proteomic profiles, SHAP interpretation, and UMAP/OPTICS clustering of protein-control profiles
organization: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; Medical College of Wisconsin; Stockholm University; University of Gothenburg

evidence.tested: MIMaL used tree-based regression and SHAP interpretation on yeast proteome/metabolome measurements, then clustered protein-control profiles across single-gene knockouts.
evidence.unknown: This was a yeast study using a prior 174-single-gene-knockout multi-omics dataset, with 348 condition profiles; it does not establish corresponding human gene functions. Five gene functions are reported validated, and the article specifically states YJR120W and YDL157C modulate mitochondrial translation. Some experimental validation used existing knockout strains and measurements; no independent replication is implied.
evidence.ai_role: A tree-based model predicted metabolite profiles from proteomic measurements; SHAP-derived protein-control values and clustering across knockout conditions were used to infer new protein–metabolite connections and gene functions. The researchers experimentally validated predicted citrate-control relationships and five gene-function predictions.
